generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The comparator for `PIPELINE_STAT_COMPARATOR` now includes `bytesProduced`. Ensure that this does not introduce any unintended sorting behavior, especially if `bytesProduced` can vary widely and affect the order of pipeline stats significantly.

In `IngestPipelineMetric.java`, the methods `preIngestBytes` and `postIngestBytes` take a parameter named `bytesReceived` and `bytesProduced`. However, these parameters are not validated. Consider adding validation to ensure that the byte counts are non-negative.

Metrics to measure ingest actions, specific to pipelines. + */ +public class IngestPipelineMetric extends IngestMetric { + + /** + * The amount of bytes received by a pipeline. + */ + private final CounterMetric bytesReceived = new CounterMetric(); + + /** + * The amount of bytes produced by a pipeline. + */ + private final CounterMetric bytesProduced = new CounterMetric(); + + /** + * Call this prior to the ingest action. + * @param bytesReceived The number of bytes received by the pipeline. + */ + void preIngestBytes(long bytesReceived) { + this.bytesReceived.inc(bytesReceived); + } + + /** + * Call this after performing the ingest action, even if the action failed. + * @param bytesProduced The number of bytes resulting from running a request in the pipeline. + */ + void postIngestBytes(long bytesProduced) { + this.bytesProduced.inc(bytesProduced); + } + + /** + * Creates a serializable representation for these metrics. + */ + IngestStats.ByteStats createByteStats() { + return new IngestStats.ByteStats(this.bytesReceived.count(), this.bytesProduced.count()); + } + +}

generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The variable `firstPipeline` is used in multiple places but is only set if there are pipelines available (`if (pipelines.hasNext() == false)`). Ensure that `firstPipeline` is not null before calling methods on it. The assertion in `#WV0AH` is good, but consider adding a similar check or handling the case where `firstPipeline` might be null.

In the test case for `ingest_info_final_pipeline`, it is expected that `ingested_in_bytes` and `produced_in_bytes` are `null`. However, if these fields are not included in the response, they will be `undefined` rather than `null`. Ensure that the API consistently returns `null` for missing values or adjust the test to check for `undefined`.

review_comment: I think it might be more clear here to put `startSize2` as the produced expected value, since the ingested and produced should be the same for failure and drop.

This comment made me aware that there might be a bug around here because I'm not sure these values are actually supposed to be equal, I think it just turns out that way because the mock processors aren't modifying the data so there's no increase in bytes.

But I dug into this a little bit more and realized I misremembered this part of the test as [this test](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/12b31e79caa67fd717ffa49166eff54e179acca9/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/ingest/IngestServiceTests.java#L181) when we brought up testing a failure
And I think parts of this test don't behave the way I thought it did (in the 3rd test the byte stats values for `_id1` hasn't increased, and in the 4th with the failure `startSize1` is equal to `endSize1`), so I'm going to dig into this a bit more

Figured out what was wrong - when the stats of a pipeline gets updated via another pipeline's stats it wasn't updating the `IngestPipelineMetric` stats, so I fixed that and changed some of the tests as necessary

Good catch on figuring out what was going on here, and fixing the `IngestPipelineMetric.add` method.

As an aside, I was at first very confused about why the `endSize1` was increasing despite the failure. Also why the `_id1` pipeline has a `failed` count of 0 in the ` assertPipelineStats` call above. I had missed that the failure-mock has an `on_failure` processor defined. When there is an on_failure processor, the resulting document does get sent to the index, so that explains why it is in the bytesProduced stat. (You may have been aware of all this already).
Yeah that was part of what led me to investigating that section, I didn't realize at first that `endSize1` was increasing there
